title: TBD Mission
description: Mission JSON contract v1. Authored by the web wizard or by hand, validated by the web validator, and executed by the TBD-Framework Enfusion loader. Missions reference registry aliases, never raw prefab GUIDs. Whole-document size ceiling: `TBD_MissionLoader.MISSION_FILE_MAX_BYTES` is `8 * 1024 * 1024` (8388608) bytes, and a profile file larger than that is refused at `LoadFromProfileFile` before `Read()`, because a truncated read would then fail JSON parse with a misleading error. JSON Schema draft 2020-12 cannot express the raw byte size of an object instance, so the ceiling is declared here as `x-tbd-missionFileMaxBytes` and enforced by the API's compiled-document validator (`GET /missions/:id/compiled`) and by the xtask schema validation, which also cross-checks the mod constant. A description alone is not a pin.

schemaVersion.description: Wire version of this document. 1.1 requires `slots[]` for per-player spawn positions. 1.2 adds the optional per-slot `y` (spawn height, metres ASL). 1.3 widens the wire once for the whole editor program: `objectives[]`, `variants`, marker style and area, `vehicles[]`, `editorTriggers[]`, per-squad waypoints and AI state, placement scatter, vehicle and entity states, environment, `missionParams[]`, zone-volume plus attacker/defender and starting-owner rules, play-area vehicle classes, and per-slot gadgets. Every 1.3 addition is optional and additive — `JsonLoadContext` ignores unknown keys — so the wire shape of a 1.1 or 1.2 document is unchanged and the bump names the widening rather than reshaping it. Both copies of `TBD_MissionValidator` (tbd-framework and tbd-export) declare SCHEMA_1_3 and `CheckSchemaVersion` admits it. The compiler emits 1.3 only when a 1.3 key actually reaches the wire: it latches on emitted slot identity plus `leaderSlotId`, and on a non-empty `vehicles[]`. A document with no 1.3 key still emits 1.1 or 1.2, so older servers are unaffected. The latch reads the serialised value, never the resolved one, so the version cannot claim 1.3 while no 1.3 key is on the wire. Like 1.1 and 1.2, a 1.3 document still requires `slots[]`. Many 1.3 fields ride the wire and are read by nothing on any shipped build; the xtask unread-fields gate asserts that per field and names the ticket that lands each reader, and a field whose reader has landed loses its row rather than keeping a re-pinned one. A 1.3 field is a definition ahead of its consumer, not a capability — the same discipline the top-level `entities` description states.

slots.description: Flattened ORBAT slot instances with exact spawn positions (required for schemaVersion 1.1).

entities.description:
World objects the MISSION places itself — vehicles, compositions, props — each named by a registry alias.

NOTHING READS THIS ON ANY BUILD SHIPPED TODAY, and a green validator is not evidence otherwise. `TBD_MissionDocumentStruct` (TBD_MissionLoader.c) declares no `entities` field, so the loader parses a mission and drops this array on the floor; no code path in the mod spawns a mission entity; `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.ArmDestroyTargets` states this in its own header and reports a destroy objective that finds no target as a first-class DIAGNOSTIC rather than faking one (TBD_ObjectivesComponent.AdvanceDestroy repeats the warning); and the editor's vehicle row is `{id, resourceName, position, squadId}` (map-engine-core doc/store.rs `add_vehicle`) with nowhere to author contents. This array is a CONTRACT AHEAD OF ITS CONSUMER — legitimate, because the schema is the shared definition the mod, the API and the editor each build against, and defining it here is what lets those three land in any order — but it is a definition, not a capability. Do not cite it as a feature.

layers.description: Tier 2 decoration layer aliases attached to this mission.

tasks.description: Authored tasks with a real state machine (schemaVersion 1.3). Distinct from `objectives[]`, which is the mission's typed objective subject, and from `winConditions.endOn`, which is the round-end trigger vocabulary. A task is what the HUD and the briefing's My Tasks list show: a primary, secondary or optional assignment that starts `assigned` and reaches exactly one terminal state, `succeeded` or `failed`. Tasks observe trigger completion through `triggerId`; they never fire `endOn` and never duplicate objective logic. Read by `TBD_TaskStateMachine` (server-authoritative transitions) and `TBD_TaskHud` (one HUD marker per assigned task, hidden once terminal). An absent array means a mission with no tasks, and the authored-block carrier then emits nothing, so byte-parity fixtures stay identical.

spawnModules.description: Authored dynamic spawn modules (schemaVersion 1.3). Each row is a wave or a garrison: `{id, kind: wave|garrison, factionKey, groupTemplate, x+z XOR zoneId, count, intervalSeconds?, maxAlive?, triggerId?}`. A wave spawns `count` groups on `intervalSeconds` (or once `triggerId` has fired) while living groups stay below `maxAlive`, which the compiler caps at 32. A garrison spawns once and holds. An absent array means a mission with no dynamic AI, and the authored-block carrier then emits nothing, so byte-parity fixtures stay identical. Read by `TBD_DynamicSpawner` in both mod trees: the server spawns groups from `groupTemplate` at (x, z) or at the named zone's centre, and clients see replicated AI. `JsonLoadContext` allocates the array when the key is absent, so presence is `Count()`.

tacticalGraphics.description: Authored tactical control measures (schemaVersion 1.3): the multi-point graphics `markers[]` structurally cannot express, because a marker is one point carrying one glyph. Each row is `{id, kind: phase_line|boundary|axis_of_advance|curved_arrow, points: [[x, z], …], label?, sideKey?, style?}`. Per-kind vertex floors live in the compiler's `min_points`: two for the open polylines, three for `curved_arrow`, because a Catmull-Rom through two points is the straight segment `axis_of_advance` already is and the two kinds would then be indistinguishable on the wire. `points` is capped at 128 vertices, because the compiled document is re-fetched by the game server and a draw tool can otherwise author a megabyte of vertices. An absent array means a mission with no control measures, and the authored-block carrier then emits nothing, so byte-parity fixtures stay identical. Nothing under the mod's `Scripts/Game/TBD` binds this key: it reaches the wire and stops there, unlike `spawnModules` and `weatherTimeline`, which the mod reads. Reaching `/compiled` takes both a named `tacticalGraphics` field on the flatten payload struct and a match arm for it; an authored-block row alone is dropped silently, because that match ends `_ => None`, and `every_authored_block_key_reaches_the_wire` is the guard that refuses a row missing either half.

objectives.description: Typed per-side objective entities (schemaVersion 1.3). Distinct from `zones[]` rows of `type: objective_*`: a zone is a volume with capture rules, whereas an objective is the mission's first-class task record — the container the editor's `objectivesById` compiles into. Read by `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry` through `TBD_ObjectiveEntityReader`, which takes a third typed `JsonLoadContext` pass over the raw document for this key, because `TBD_MissionDocumentStruct` declares no field for it and `JsonLoadContext` binds by member name, so the primary loader structurally cannot see it. The compiler does not emit the key on `/compiled`, so the only document that reaches the reader is a hand-staged 1.3 one; `golden-missions/schema-1_3-wire-fields.json` is that staged case. Each row is one objective with a uniform attribute spine (id, type, side, zoneId, label), optional per-side `framing` (the attacker and defender readings of the same objective — never two rows for one objective; see `$defs/objective`), and the capture, defend and height model carried on `zoneRules`: attackerCount, defenderCount, advantagePercent, minHeight, maxHeight and startingOwner, whose degenerate one-against-one case is a zone's `contestable`. Distinct from `winConditions.endOn`: that is the win trigger vocabulary, this is the objective subject it fires on.

vehicles.description: Mission-placed vehicle roster (schemaVersion 1.3), the compile half of the crewed-vehicle path. A vehicle is not an `entities[]` alias row: `#/$defs/alias` is `^(kit|comp|veh|preset|layer|prop|item):[a-z0-9_]+$` and the mod's `Data/registry.json` holds exactly one `veh:` row, so routing crewed vehicles through `entities[]` would silently substitute a ten-tonne vehicle. This is a document root key plus its own `$def`, carrying seats and crew references onto the wire. Read by `TBD_MissionVehicleStruct`, bound through `TBD_MissionDocumentStruct.vehicles` and seated by `TBD_SpawnManager` once the slot bodies materialise. One authored vehicle emits two rows — this roster row and an `entities[]` alias row — and `entities[]` is already spawned by `SpawnMissionEntities()`, so `uid` is the join key the roster reader claims on; without that claim every crewed vehicle reaches the world twice. Compiled from the editor's `vehiclesById`, the sibling of the payload's own top-level `vehicles` bag, and this is the declared contract shape.

editorTriggers.description: Editor-authored trigger entities: an activation model (condition, repeat, timeout, owner side) plus an effects model (schemaVersion 1.3). The key is `editorTriggers`, not `triggers`, deliberately. The compiler already emits a win-condition trigger vocabulary as `winConditions.endOn` (`time_limit`, `faction_eliminated` and so on), and an editor trigger is a different object with a different lifecycle — an authored condition-to-effect rule, not a round-end predicate. Collapsing them onto one `triggers` key would leave a reader unable to tell a win predicate from an authored rule, so they are named apart on the wire: `winConditions.endOn` keeps the win vocabulary and `editorTriggers[]` carries the trigger runtime. The editor payload carries these as `triggersById`; this is the compiled, declared shape. Read by `TBD_TriggerRuntime`, which takes a second typed `JsonLoadContext` pass over the raw document for this key, because `TBD_MissionDocumentStruct` declares no field for it and `JsonLoadContext` binds by member name. Geometry rides the zone draw tool, so a trigger's area is a `zones[]` row referenced by `zoneId` rather than re-declared here.

variants.description: The named-variant registry for conditional inclusion (schemaVersion 1.3). It generalises the by-hand layer convention a template ships when it names modes and a setup script deletes every object and marker belonging to the modes not picked, which makes a layer name a hard runtime contract. Here each variant is declared once by `id`, and any variant-gated subtree elsewhere in the document — an objective, a vehicle, an entity, a zone, a trigger — references it through `variantId`; the compiler emits that subtree only when the variant is selected. Declaring variants centrally is what makes the `variantId` predicate validatable: an unknown id is catchable rather than a free string. `TBD_MissionLoader` evaluates the registry at `ParseMissionJson` (`$profile:TBD_VariantConfig.json` `activeVariants[]`, else the rows whose `default` is true) and drops excluded subtrees before spawn. `objectives[]` and `editorTriggers[]` are re-parsed from `GetRawJson()`, so they are gated in their own passes.

missionParams.description: First-class launch-time mission parameters (schemaVersion 1.3): a mission carries named parameters chosen at launch rather than baked in at authoring time — name, i18n title key, value list, display list, default, and the symbol the mission consumes each one through. This models Arma's `class Params`, the mechanism that lets one artefact serve as training server, briefing room, mod-check sandbox and match. Read by `TBD_MissionParams` in both mod trees; the launch selection comes from `$profile:TBD_MissionParams.json`, else the authored default. The compiler does not emit the array onto `/compiled`.

alias.description: Registry alias resolved by the framework registry to a prefab GUID.

cargoContainer.description: Worn container a cargo row is inserted into. Closed vocabulary: unlike `kit:` and `preset:` aliases these four are fixed by the engine's worn-garment areas rather than by extensible content, so the enum can never fight the registry. `TBD_LoadoutEquipHelper.GarmentForContainer` maps exactly these to LoadoutVestArea (plus LoadoutArmoredVestSlotArea), LoadoutJacketArea, LoadoutPantsArea and LoadoutBackpackArea, and the Arsenal UI offers exactly these. Without the enum a typo validates clean and then degrades at runtime: `GarmentForContainer` returns null and `InsertCargo` falls through to `TryInsertItem` anywhere, so the cargo lands in the wrong place instead of failing. `armoredVest` is deliberately not a key — it shares the vest container (single-vest collapse).

wireSafeString.description: A free-text authored string that reaches a delimited wire and therefore may not contain a character that frames one. `TBD_SpawnManager.BuildSlotRoster`, `TBD_BriefingData`, `TBD_LobbyData` and `TBD_AdminData` all serialise to tab-separated fields joined by newlines, so a TAB in an authored value opens a new column and a CR or LF opens a new row. The consequence runs end to end: a callsign authored `AL<TAB>PHA` is a schema-valid mission that produces a seven-field roster row, passes the consumer's `< 6` arity guard, shifts every column, renders `role` as `PHA`, makes the real role read as the state (so the seat matches neither OPEN nor DEAD and becomes unselectable), and parses `holderId` from `"OPEN".ToInt()` = 0. The mod also sanitises at the source (`TBD_SpawnManager.RosterField` and `TBD_BriefingData.Sanitise`, each substituting a space and warning once per distinct value) and the lobby parser is pinned to exact arity, so this pattern is defence in depth — but the schema is where the class dies, because a rewritten field is still a field the author did not write. The pattern bans the whole C0 control block plus DEL rather than only the three framing characters: a strict superset at zero cost to legitimate authoring, a closed character class that cannot drift, and one that covers the unsanitised siblings — NUL is a C-string terminator on a byte-indexed engine (`string.Length()` counts bytes here), and VT and FF are treated as line breaks by enough downstream tooling to be the next hazard. Deliberately not banned: `.`, because the per-field marker `TBD_BriefingData.FIELD_MARK` is bijective by construction, with `Unmark(Field(x)) == Sanitise(x)` for every x including `.` and the empty string; `~`, the retired `TBD_LobbyData.EMPTY` sentinel, forbidding which would enshrine a convention the tree abandoned; `:`, load-bearing inside `slot.id` (`{faction}:{groupCallsign}:{role}:{index}`); and zero-width joiners, bidi and RTL overrides and U+2028/U+2029, which are a display-spoofing class rather than a wire-framing one — none can shift a column, an open-ended Unicode blocklist is exactly the drifting vocabulary a closed class refuses to become, and folding two unrelated defects behind one pattern means a failure no longer names its cause. Briefing prose (`briefing.situation`, `briefing.mission`, `briefing.execution`) is deliberately excluded from this `$ref`: it rides no delimited wire, because `TBD_BriefingService` ships it as parallel `array<string>` RPC parameters, so an embedded newline there is legitimate authoring rather than a hazard.

id.description: Content-hash id assigned on publish. Optional in hand-written drafts.

terrain.description: Must match a framework scenario / terrain key.

environment.description: Mission environment. `fog`, `wind` and `viewDistance` ride the wire (schemaVersion 1.3) as the scenario-side environment axes. The authoring path lands separately, so read this before adding an editor control: the frontend's `keys_nothing_reads_are_not_authored` test names `viewDistance`, `thermals`, `windDirDeg`, `fog` and `wind` as keys the editor must not author. That test gates authoring, not the wire — the mod reader comes first and the control second. Read by `TBD_EnvironmentReader` in both mod trees, which binds `fog`, `wind`, `windDirDeg` and `viewDistance` when they are authored. Editor controls stay refused until the authoring slice lands.

windDirDeg.description: Wind direction in degrees. Read by `TBD_EnvironmentReader`, and reapplied in `TBD_FrameworkManager` weather setup through `SetWindDirectionOverride` with an ABSENT sentinel for the unauthored case.

fog.description: Fog density, 0 (clear) to 1 (thickest), matching Eden's normalised scenario fog. Read by `TBD_EnvironmentReader`.

wind.description: Wind strength in m/s; direction is the sibling `windDirDeg`. Read by `TBD_EnvironmentReader`.

viewDistance.description: Terrain and object view distance in metres. Read by `TBD_EnvironmentReader`. Deliberately not authored by the editor: the frontend environment inspector asserts the key stays un-authored, and the editor control is a later slice.

orbat.description: Per-faction order of battle. Keys must match faction keys.

callsign.description: The ORBAT-side CAUSE of slot.groupCallsign. flatten.rs copies this verbatim into slot.groupCallsign and interpolates it into slot.id, and nothing re-validates the compiled document — so constraining only the slot fields would forbid the symptom while permitting the cause.

combatMode.description: Group rules of engagement (schemaVersion 1.3), on TBD's own ladder from blue (never fire) to red (open fire, engage at will). These are TBD vocabulary mapped onto `EAIGroupCombatMode` (HOLD_FIRE / RETURN_FIRE / FIRE_AT_WILL). Read by `TBD_GroupState`, and applied only once the group has been AI-enabled.

behaviour.description: Group behaviour state (schemaVersion 1.3) in TBD vocabulary: careless, safe, aware, combat, stealth. Read by `TBD_WaypointRuntime` as a waypoint override and by `TBD_GroupState` as the group default. A waypoint that authors behaviour wins over the group default.

formation.description: Group movement formation (schemaVersion 1.3). The enum tokens are shared vocabulary: the editor's `force_to_formation` action and Transform submenu consume them, with geometry from `formation_offsets`. Read by `TBD_GroupState`, which maps the engine's four-name set directly and folds the extra names onto Wedge, Line, Column and StaggeredColumn.

speedMode.description: Group movement speed mode (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_WaypointRuntime` as a waypoint override and by `TBD_GroupState` as the group default, which binds with DEFAULT origin so a waypoint `speedMode` wins.

waypoints.description: Per-squad waypoint list (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_WaypointRuntime`. `TBD_SpawnManager` opens the AI spawn gate only for waypointed groups. The group's own `combatMode` and `formation` are read by `TBD_GroupState`.

placementRadius.description: Scatter radius in metres (schemaVersion 1.3): the group's members are scattered within this radius of its authored position at spawn, and 0 or absent means exact placement. Read by `TBD_PlacementScatter`. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader. Group scatter is a shared offset because groups carry no authored x/z on the wire. The 2D top-down editor is the surface where the scatter circle is drawable.

placementShape.description: Scatter area shape for this group's `placementRadius` (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_PlacementScatter`. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader.

variantId.description: Conditional inclusion (schemaVersion 1.3). When set, this group is emitted only if the named `variants[]` entry is selected. `TBD_MissionLoader` drops the subtree when the named variant is inactive.

leaderSlotId.description: The TBD-only key naming which slot leads this squad (schemaVersion 1.3). It references `slots[].uid`, a durable identity, because `id` is derived and shifts under role renames, reorders and deletes (see the `slot.id` description). Squad leadership is a per-squad fact, so it lives here on the wire ORBAT group in one copy rather than denormalised onto every `slots[]` entry, where N copies could disagree with no schema able to catch it; the editor likewise authors it once per squad at `/editor/squads/*/leaderSlotId`. Read through `TBD_MissionLoader.GetSquadLeaderSlot` and `IsSquadLeader`, which resolve it through the uid-aware slot lookup and then re-check that the seat belongs to this squad: slot uids are unique document-wide, so a `leaderSlotId` copied between squads resolves cleanly to a seat in the wrong one and nothing downstream could notice. A cross-squad reference yields no leader rather than a guessed one.

slot.description: The ORBAT-side CAUSE of slot.role — flatten.rs copies it into slot.role and into slot.id. Same reasoning as group.callsign.

radio.description: Net ids this role spawns tuned to.

id.description: Human-readable slot label: {faction}:{groupCallsign}:{role}:{index}. DERIVED each compile — shifts under role renames/reorders/deletes; key durable references on uid instead. Reaches the roster wire as column 1 via slot.Key() when uid is absent.

uid.description: Stable slot identity (B1): the editor document's slot id, carried verbatim so the identity survives recompiles and ORBAT edits. Spawn points, rosters and logs key on this. Optional for pre-B1 documents. (Named uid, not ref — ref is an EnforceScript keyword.) Reaches the roster wire as column 1 — slot.Key() prefers it over id.

y.description: Optional spawn height, metres ASL (schemaVersion 1.2). Maps from the editor's position.z. Absent → the loader uses terrain surface Y.

loadout.description: Optional per-slot Arsenal loadout, flattened from the editor's SlotLoadout v2. It is additive data: `JsonLoadContext` readers ignore unknown keys, so it ships without a schemaVersion bump and the mod loader's 1.1/1.2 allowlist still admits the document. The kit alias stays authoritative for the base character, and the loadout layers on top of it.

gear.description: Fixed gear ResourceNames. Wear derivation: jacket → uniform, armoredVest else vest → vest (single-vest collapse), headCover → helmet; pants, boots, handwear and backpack are copied verbatim. Weapons: all four editor weapon slots are carried, each selected by the exact (slotIndex, slotType) pair the Arsenal authors — (0, primary) → primary, (1, primary) → launcher, (2, secondary) → handgun, (3, grenade) → throwable — and each keeps the editor's own key name so the compiled document reads the same words the Arsenal UI shows. `optic` and `magazine` ride the (0, primary) rifle alone; the other three weapons carry no sub-slots. Empty slots are omitted, never written as empty strings. `attachments[]` is optional and holds wire-safe ResourceNames from the (0, primary) SlotLoadout v2 edges; it is omitted when empty.

attachments.description: Optional primary-rifle Arsenal attachment ResourceNames, copied from the SlotLoadout v2 `weapons[].attachments` edges on (slotIndex 0, slotType primary). Omitted when empty. Mounted by `TBD_LoadoutEquipHelper` after optic and magazine.

cargo.description: Container cargo rows in the loadout-export v2 shape, `{container, item, qty}`, copied verbatim from the editor cargo. Omitted when empty.

callsign.description: A per-slot display callsign (schemaVersion 1.3), distinct from `groupCallsign` (the ORBAT group name) and from `id` (the derived label). Bound on `TBD_MissionSlotStruct` and logged per identified seat. Reforger exposes no replicated free-text name on a character — `CharacterIdentityComponent.SetIdentityFromIDs` takes indices into a faction identity table — so this value reaches every surface holding the slot and the server log, and is deliberately not pushed onto the spawned entity. Constrained to `wireSafeString` because it reaches the same tab-delimited roster wire as `id`.

rank.description: Character rank on TBD's own ladder, private through colonel (schemaVersion 1.3). The engine type is `SCR_ECharacterRank`, whose unprefixed members are PRIVATE, CORPORAL, SERGEANT, LIEUTENANT, CAPTAIN, MAJOR and COLONEL (plus RENEGADE and GENERAL, which TBD does not author), applied through `SCR_CharacterRankComponent.SetCharacterRank` and replicated. TBD's ladder is an exact lowercase subset, and the names here are the contract. A kit prefab with no rank component is reported at WARNING rather than silently dropping the authored rank.

stance.description: Initial spawn pose (schemaVersion 1.3). Applied through `CharacterControllerComponent.SetStanceChange` on every spawn including respawn, because a fresh body inherits nothing.

unitName.description: A per-slot unit name (schemaVersion 1.3). Bound on the slot and logged, not pushed onto the spawned entity, for the same reason as `callsign` — read that description. Constrained to `wireSafeString` because it reaches a delimited wire.

tag.description: The TBD-only slot tag key (schemaVersion 1.3), mirroring the ORBAT-slot `tag` the events path already carries. Bound on the slot and logged. Like `callsign` and `unitName` it has no engine target that reaches a client, so it is not pushed onto the spawned entity.

placementRadius.description: Scatter radius in metres (schemaVersion 1.3): this slot is scattered within this radius of its authored (x, z) at spawn, and 0 or absent means exact placement. Read by `TBD_PlacementScatter` (`ForSlot`, from `SpawnSlotBody`). The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader.

placementShape.description: Scatter area shape for this slot's `placementRadius` (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_PlacementScatter`. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader.

gadgets.description: Which personal gadgets this player spawns with — map, compass, watch, GPS, radio (schemaVersion 1.3). This is the Eden General-States model that lets a scenario decide a player's gadgets. Read by `TBD_GadgetFlags` in both mod trees: bound from the mission loader and applied after spawn. The binding is a `map<string,bool>`, so an empty map (`Count() == 0`) keeps the kit defaults and each flag is resolved by `Find`. The compiler does not emit `slot.gadgets`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader. Authoring `gps: true` cannot add a GPS, because the TBD registry holds no GPS item.

variantId.description: Conditional inclusion (schemaVersion 1.3). When set, this slot is emitted only if the named `variants[]` entry is selected. `TBD_MissionLoader` drops the subtree when the named variant is inactive.

radioPlan.description: Shared contract consumed by the framework and the partner VOIP bridge. Nets map to voice channels.

nets.description: Radio nets in this plan. `maxItems` 32 pins `TBD_RadioPlan.MAX_NETS`: the mod truncates to the first 32 valid nets and warns, so without this bound a document can validate and still drop authored channels.

label.description: Display label for the net. `maxLength` 48 pins `TBD_RadioPlan.MAX_LABEL_CHARS`: the mod truncates over-long labels through `CapLabel`, so without this bound a document can validate and still show a shortened channel name.

range.description: Which radio class this net prefers. Enfusion exposes exactly two gadget types — `EGadgetType.RADIO` (handheld) and `EGadgetType.RADIO_BACKPACK` — and the mod wire is a 0/1 flag (`TBD_RadioService.LongRangeFlag` into `m_aLongRange`): `short` means handheld (flag 0), `long` means backpack (flag 1). There is no third hardware class, so a value meaning 'either' is rejected here rather than kept as a synonym that looks distinct while collapsing onto the same flag as `short`.

shape.description: Exactly one of circle or polygon.

markerArea.description: The extent of an AREA marker (schemaVersion 1.3): a superset of `#/$defs/shape` (circle | polygon) that also expresses the rectangle and ellipse extents Eden's second marker model needs and `#/$defs/shape` cannot, since a rect or ellipse has a centre, half-extents and a rotation rather than a radius or a ring. Exactly one of circle, polygon, rectangle or ellipse. This def, not `shape` (the icon-glyph selector on `marker`), is the authoritative geometry of an area marker: when `marker.area` is present the marker is an area marker and `marker.shape` is ignored — a precedence rule stated on both. On the wire only; no mod-side reader binds it.

rectExtent.description: The extent of a rectangle or ellipse area marker (schemaVersion 1.3): a centre `(x, z)`, half-extents `halfWidth` and `halfHeight` in metres (so the full box is 2·halfWidth by 2·halfHeight), and a `rotationDeg`. Shared by the `rectangle` and `ellipse` arms of `#/$defs/markerArea` — an ellipse is the same bounding box read as an oval, matching Eden's rectangular and elliptical marker areas.

label.description: Optional human name. Reaches the briefing Z record via TBD_BriefingService.PrettyZoneTitle, which falls back to type + zone.id when this is empty — so both keys are on that wire. No minLength: an empty label is a committed golden (empty-warning-fields.json) and means "use the fallback".

variantId.description: Conditional inclusion (schemaVersion 1.3). When set, this zone is emitted only if the named `variants[]` entry is selected. `TBD_MissionLoader` drops the subtree when the named variant is inactive.

zoneRules.description: Zone-type specific rules. Optional as a whole — a zone that authors no `rules` runs entirely on the defaults named per key below. This is a closed vocabulary because both readers are typed: Enfusion's `JsonLoadContext` maps JSON keys onto named class fields, so a key the class does not declare is invisible to it — not rejected, not logged, simply absent. `TBD_ZoneRegistry.ResolveRules` then reports that it could read no rule this build understands, which is equally true of a zone that authored nothing and of one that authored `graceSecconds`, and a typed parser cannot tell those apart. That makes this schema the only place a misspelled rule key can be caught, so `additionalProperties` is false and every key the mod reads is declared here; adding a rule to the vocabulary is a field in the reader plus a property here. The vocabulary is flat and is not narrowed by `zone.type`, because neither reader is type-conditional: `TBD_MissionZoneRulesStruct` is parsed for every zone and `TBD_ObjectiveRulesStruct` runs a second pass over every zone in the same document, so `captureSeconds` on a boundary zone parses and is ignored. Narrowing per type here would declare a rule the runtime does not enforce; the per-key descriptions name the consuming zone type instead, and `TBD_ZoneRegistry.ResolveRules` only suppresses its diagnostics for types it does not enforce rather than rejecting the keys. Each minimum below is the reader's own error branch (`< 0` or `<= 0`), where an out-of-range value is discarded in favour of the default, and each maximum pins the matching mod sanity ceiling: `graceSeconds` at `TBD_ZoneRegistry.MAX_GRACE_SECONDS` (3600), and `captureSeconds`, `neutralizeSeconds` and `holdSeconds` at `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS` (21600). Encoding those ceilings here means a document cannot validate and still be clamped at runtime. On presence: numeric and string keys carry an ABSENT sentinel (-1e6, and -1 for the one integer, because `targetCount: 0` is meaningful) so a bad authored value is reported as an error instead of being mistaken for 'not authored'. Bools cannot carry one — there is no third value — so for the four booleans 'absent' and 'authored false' are indistinguishable at runtime; each bool's default is the value an author gets by writing nothing, so nothing is lost behaviourally.

graceSeconds.description: Play area (`boundary`, `base_protection`). Seconds a player may remain in violation before `penalty` is applied. Bound by `TBD_MissionZoneRulesStruct` and resolved by `TBD_ZoneRegistry`; a negative value is rejected in favour of the default. The `maximum` of 3600 pins `TBD_ZoneRegistry.MAX_GRACE_SECONDS` — above that the mod warns and falls back to 30 s.

warnEverySeconds.description: PLAY AREA (`boundary`, `base_protection`). How often, in seconds, a player in violation is told. Read at TBD_MissionLoader.c:103, resolved at TBD_ZoneRegistry.c:401-413. Zero would mean "warn every frame", so the reader requires > 0.

penalty.description: PLAY AREA (`boundary`, `base_protection`). What happens once `graceSeconds` elapses. `none` tracks server-side and says nothing; `warn` tells the player and never acts; `kill` is TERMINAL under one life. Read at TBD_MissionLoader.c:104, matched against TBD_ZoneRegistry.PENALTY_* at :419-438 (enum TBD_EZonePenalty, TBD_Zone.c:36-41). A value outside this set resolves to `warn`, never `kill` — the mod refuses to guess toward ending a player's only life, and this enum is what stops a typo getting that far.

captureSeconds.description: `objective_capture`. Seconds of uninterrupted presence needed to take a NEUTRAL objective. Bound by `TBD_ObjectiveRulesStruct` and resolved by `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry`. Absent defaults rather than going inert: an objective nobody chose the length of is still playable, whereas an inert one takes the `all_objectives_captured` trigger with it and the round can no longer be won. The `maximum` of 21600 pins `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS`.

neutralizeSeconds.description: `objective_capture`. Seconds of presence needed to tear a HELD objective back to neutral. Bound by `TBD_ObjectiveRulesStruct` and resolved by `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry`. It defaults to `captureSeconds`, a symmetric 1:1 rate, so there is no literal default to state here. `0` is legal and means instant — a single-stage capture. The `maximum` of 21600 pins `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS`.

contestable.description: `objective_capture`. Does an enemy inside stop the capture? True freezes progress while two sides are present; false resolves by weight of numbers and freezes only on an exact tie. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:97, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:476; meaning fixed at TBD_Objective.c:262-299.

onEmpty.description: `objective_capture`. What happens to partial progress when NOBODY is inside. `hold` keeps it; `decay` bleeds it back at `decayRate`. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:95, matched against TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.ON_EMPTY_* at :478-492. An unrecognised value resolves to `hold`.

decayRate.description: `objective_capture`, and meaningful only with `onEmpty: "decay"`. Progress-seconds lost per real second while decaying; `1` bleeds at the same rate progress accrues. Bound by `TBD_ObjectiveRulesStruct` and resolved by `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry`.

holdSeconds.description: `objective_hold_until`, where it is effectively required. Seconds the zone's `faction` must hold the ground. Bound by `TBD_ObjectiveRulesStruct` and resolved by `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry`. There is deliberately no default: a hold is the length of the round (`last-stand-at-montfort.json` authors 2700 s inside a 3000 s limit), so guessing it means guessing when the round ends and who won. An `objective_hold_until` with no readable `holdSeconds` goes inert and reports why. It is not declared `required` here because the readers do not reject the document — see the `$def` description on why this vocabulary is not narrowed by zone type. The `maximum` of 21600 pins `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.MAX_DURATION_SECONDS`; above that the mod marks the objective inert.

pauseOnEnemy.description: `objective_hold_until`. An enemy inside PAUSES the hold clock. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:98, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:553.

resetOnEnemy.description: `objective_hold_until`. An enemy inside RESETS the hold clock to zero. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:99, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:554.

requireHolderPresent.description: `objective_hold_until`. The hold clock only runs while a friendly is inside. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:100, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:555.

targetAlias.description: `objective_destroy`, where it is effectively required. Registry alias of the thing that must be destroyed, for example `comp:ammo_cache`. Bound by `TBD_ObjectiveRulesStruct` and resolved by `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.ArmDestroyTargets`; an `objective_destroy` with no readable alias goes inert, because there is nothing to watch. Constrained to the same `#/$defs/alias` form as `entity.alias`, since it resolves through the same framework registry. `TBD_MissionDocumentStruct` models `entities[]` and `SpawnMissionEntities` places resolvable rows after parse, and `ArmDestroyTargets` then AABB-queries the zone. Inert reasons distinguish an unresolved registry alias, no matching `entities[]` row, out-of-zone authorship, and a spawn or query miss.

targetCount.description: `objective_destroy`. How many matching targets must die. `0` (or absent) means ALL of them, which is why the reader's absent-sentinel for this key is -1 rather than 0. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:92, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:577-588.

points.description: EVERY objective type. Score carried and reported on completion. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:90, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:399-410. No default is stated because no end trigger in this build consumes it — it is transported, not scored.

announceEverySeconds.description: EVERY objective type. How often a player standing on the objective is told the progress. Read at TBD_ObjectiveRules.c:89, resolved at TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.c:412-423. No single default is stated because the default is per zone type: 15 s for `objective_capture` (DEFAULT_CAPTURE_ANNOUNCE_SECONDS) and 60 s for `objective_hold_until` (DEFAULT_HOLD_ANNOUNCE_SECONDS).

attackerCount.description: `objective_capture` (schemaVersion 1.3). How many attackers must be inside the volume for capture progress to accrue. A zone's `contestable: bool` is the degenerate one-against-one case of this plus `defenderCount`. Read by `TBD_ZoneVolume` through the `TBD_MissionZoneRulesStruct` bind and applied by `TBD_ObjectivesComponent`. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader. Absent means 1; an authored 0 turns the count gate off.

defenderCount.description: `objective_capture` and `objective_hold_until` (schemaVersion 1.3). How many defenders must be inside the volume to hold it. Read by `TBD_ZoneVolume` through the loader bind and applied by `TBD_ObjectivesComponent`. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader.

advantagePercent.description: `objective_capture` (schemaVersion 1.3). The numeric advantage, in percent, one side needs over the other before capture progresses. Read by `TBD_ZoneVolume` through the loader bind and applied by `TBD_ObjectivesComponent`. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader.

minHeight.description: The objective volume's LOWER bound (schemaVersion 1.3), in metres above terrain (AGL), evaluated at each tested entity's own ground position — not ASL, and not anchored to the zone centre. Axis and evaluation point are stated because a slope makes the two readings diverge by tens of metres, which is precisely the behaviour these bounds exist for: a small negative minimum reaches basements under the entity, while a bounded maximum excludes aircraft overhead, both judged per entity — so a polygon zone needs no separate height anchor, since each entity supplies its own terrain reference. Together with `maxHeight` this makes an objective a 3D volume rather than a flat footprint. Read by `TBD_ZoneVolume`, AGL at each entity's own ground. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader.

maxHeight.description: The objective volume's UPPER bound (schemaVersion 1.3), in metres above terrain (AGL), evaluated at each tested entity's own ground position — the same axis and evaluation point as `minHeight`: AGL per entity, not ASL, and not anchored to the zone centre. Its practical job is to exclude aircraft overhead. Read by `TBD_ZoneVolume` through the loader bind and applied by `TBD_ObjectivesComponent`. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader.

startingOwner.description: Which faction holds this objective at round start (schemaVersion 1.3). Constrained to `factionKey`, because it names a `factions[].key`. Read by `TBD_ZoneVolume` through the loader bind and applied by `TBD_ObjectivesComponent`. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader.

vehicleClasses.description: Play area (`boundary`, `base_protection`), schemaVersion 1.3: which vehicle classes the play-area rule applies to — the remaining axis on a play-area model that otherwise carries graceSeconds, warnEverySeconds and penalty. The case it exists for is an aircraft exemption: a play-zone rule whose air flag is off lets aircraft leave the area while ground vehicles and infantry may not. There is no `minItems`, so all three presence cases are legal and are defined here. Absent means the rule applies to everything — every vehicle class and infantry are confined. A non-empty list restricts the rule to exactly the classes named, so omitting `aircraft` from the list is how the aircraft exemption is authored. An empty list `[]` is the explicit inverse of absent: the rule applies to no vehicle class, so nothing is confined by it. `[]` is therefore not the same as absent, and this clause is what defines it. Read by `TBD_PlayAreaVehicleAxis` through the loader bind and applied by `TBD_ZoneRegistry`. The compiler clones `zones[].rules` as an opaque JSON value. On the mod side an authored `[]` and an absent key both bind as `Count() == 0` and confine everyone, so the schema's inverse case is unreachable at runtime.

entity.description: One mission-placed world object. Read the top-level `entities` description before building on this — nothing on any shipped build spawns one.

uid.description: Stable identity for this entity (schemaVersion 1.3), carried verbatim from the editor — the same role `slot.uid` and `vehicle.uid` play. It is the join key between the two rows one authored vehicle emits: a placed vehicle compiles to an `entities[]` alias row AND a `vehicles[]` roster row, deliberately, and the mod already spawns `entities[]` through `TBD_MissionLoader.SpawnMissionEntities`, so without a shared key a roster reader would spawn every crewed vehicle a second time. A reader dedupes on `entity.uid == vehicle.uid`. Optional: an entity nothing references needs no uid, and a blank or wire-unsafe authored id yields no key rather than a repaired one.

lock.description: Vehicle lock state (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_VehicleState` on the `vehicles[]` roster, through `LockPilotControls`. An `entities[]`-only row with no roster twin is not read.

fuel.description: Vehicle fuel fraction, 0 to 1 (full), schemaVersion 1.3. Read by `TBD_VehicleState` on the `vehicles[]` roster. An `entities[]`-only row with no roster twin is not read.

ammo.description: Vehicle ammunition fraction, 0 to 1 (full), schemaVersion 1.3. Read by `TBD_VehicleState` on the `vehicles[]` roster, covering current magazines and cargo. An `entities[]`-only row with no roster twin is not read.

health.description: Initial health fraction, 0 (destroyed) to 1 (pristine), schemaVersion 1.3. Read by `TBD_EntityState` through `DamageManagerComponent.SetHealthScaled` on spawned `entities[]` bodies. Unset leaves the prefab default. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`, so hand-staged 1.3 JSON is what reaches the reader.

allowDamage.description: Whether this entity may take damage at all — Eden's invincibility toggle (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_EntityState` through `EnableDamageHandling(true)`, and only when bound true: a bool carries no absent sentinel, so an authored false and an omitted key bind identically. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`.

showModel.description: Whether the entity's model is visible — Eden's show/hide (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_EntityState` through `SetFlags(VISIBLE)`, and only when bound true: an authored false (hide) cannot be distinguished from an omitted key. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`.

size.description: Uniform scale multiplier for the placed object, where 1 is native size (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_EntityState` through `IEntity.SetScale`. Unset leaves the prefab scale. Distinct from `marker.size`, which shares the spelling and is a different field. The compiler omits the entity key on `/compiled`.

stamina.description: Whether stamina is enabled for a character entity (schemaVersion 1.3). Bound as an identifier on `TBD_EntityState`, but Reforger exposes no per-character stamina enable toggle (`BaseStaminaComponent` offers `GetStamina` only), so an authored true is logged and skipped. The compiler omits the key on `/compiled`.

variantId.description: Conditional inclusion (schemaVersion 1.3). When set, this entity is emitted only if the named `variants[]` entry is selected. `TBD_MissionLoader` drops the subtree when the named variant is inactive.

entityInventory.description: What an author puts INTO this entity's own storage — the vehicle and crate answer to the question `slot.loadout.cargo` answers for a worn garment. This is not a `cargoContainer` row: `#/$defs/cargoContainer` is [vest, pants, jacket, backpack] and is closed by the engine's worn-garment areas rather than by content, since `TBD_LoadoutEquipHelper.GarmentForContainer` resolves each key to a LoadoutArea on a CHARACTER. Widening that enum to admit `vehicle` or `crate` is deliberately declined: a vehicle is not a garment, and an enum meaning 'worn area' cannot also mean 'any object with storage' without losing the property that made it safe to close. Here the container IS the entity, which is why these rows carry no `container` key at all — there is exactly one storage to address and `alias` already names it. No sub-compartment vocabulary is invented either, because naming vehicle bays would be exactly the extensible-content enum that must stay open. There are deliberately no capacity fields: the limits already exist per prefab in `registry-items.schema.json` (`max_weight_kg`, `max_volume_cm3`, `cargo_grid_w`, `cargo_grid_h`) across the vehicle and crate rows, and the join is live — `entity.alias` resolves through `registry.json` to a ResourceName and that keys the registry-items row. Restating any of it here would be a second source of truth for a number the mission does not own, and the copy would go stale the first time the prefab is rebalanced: the mission says what goes in, the registry says how much fits. Rows are additive, never a wipe. A row is INSERTED into whatever the prefab already spawns carrying — the same layering `slot.loadout` does over the kit alias — so absent and `[]` mean the same thing: leave the prefab's own contents alone. An 'empty it first' semantic would need its own key and must never be spelled as the absence of this one, because that would silently redefine every mission authored without it. Nothing consumes this key yet; see the top-level `entities` description. It defines the contract, it does not deliver the capability.

item.description: Enfusion ResourceName of the prefab to insert. Same vocabulary as `slot.loadout.cargo[].item` on purpose — ONE item spelling per document, so a given rifle is not a registry alias when it sits in a crate and a ResourceName when it sits in a vest.

qty.description: UNIT COUNT, not a stack size. The character-side reader this mirrors (TBD_LoadoutEquipHelper.InsertCargo) spawns the prefab once per unit and inserts each one separately; an entity-side reader has the same engine primitive available against the entity's storage (SCR_InventoryStorageManagerComponent.TryInsertItemInStorage).

objective.description: One typed objective entity (schemaVersion 1.3). Read the top-level `objectives` description first, including which half of the path is live: `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry` reads the key, and the compiler does not emit it on `/compiled`. This def carries the uniform attribute spine every objective shares — id, type, side, zoneId, label — plus the fields below. `type` is the SUBJECT vocabulary (what kind of task), distinct from `winConditions.endOn`'s TRIGGER vocabulary (when the round ends) and from `zone.type`'s volume-with-rules. Capture-tuning numbers (attackerCount, defenderCount, advantagePercent, minHeight, maxHeight, startingOwner) live on `zoneRules` where the runtime already reads them; this def carries the objective's identity, not a second copy of those numbers. One entity, two framings — not two rows: an objective reads differently to attacker and defender (different task text and titles, separate My Tasks and Ally Tasks trees), but that is ONE objective with per-side framing, authored through the optional `framing` object below. A document must NOT carry two `objectives[]` rows that are 'the same objective' for opposite sides. Splitting an objective across rows brings four defects with it — positional identity, two halves linked only by a shared prefix or target, nothing validating that both halves exist, and tooling that divides objective counts by two so a forgotten half yields a fractional count — and TBD's stable `uid` and derived `id` already make the positional-identity defect unreachable.

type.description: The task kind. Named apart from `zone.type` (which is the enforcement volume) and `winConditions.endOn` (the round-end predicate). `defend` is a FRAMING of the same objective a `capture` presents to the other side — it does NOT license a second row for the opposing side (see the def description: one entity, two framings).

side.description: Which faction must complete this objective (a `factions[].key`): it attacks for capture/destroy and defends for hold/defend. The other side's reading is authored via `framing`, not a separate objective row. When side is absent, framing uses the zone's faction. An explicitly authored side naming no mission faction yields the neutral label and no task body for every viewer, without falling back to the zone's faction. The zone's faction remains its ownership restriction.

zoneId.description: The `zones[].id` that gives this objective its geometry and capture rules. An objective points at its enforcement volume rather than restating the shape, so the drawn zone is the single source of the footprint.

label.description: The objective's neutral display name. Per-side task text/titles are authored in `framing`; this is the side-agnostic label.

framing.description: The per-side framing of this one objective, implemented as one entity rather than two modules. Optional; when absent the objective reads the same to everyone, off `label` and `type`. Each side gets its own task title and text — 'Seize the hilltop' to the attacker, 'Hold the hilltop' to the defender — from a single objective, so there is never a second row to keep in sync. `TBD_Objective.RoleOf` derives the viewer's role from the one row and `TitleFor` / `TaskTextFor` render it, so board lines read per side. The reader also refuses the shape this def forbids: two `objectives[]` rows naming one `zoneId` raise a load warning quoting the ban, and the first row wins.

lock.description: Whether this objective is locked at round start. The semantics are inferred: the parameter name and its observed values are hard evidence from the source corpus, but the reading of what a locked objective does is inference and a reader must not treat it as fact. It is parsed and reported, deliberately not enforced: the parameter says 'at round start' and the corpus holds no evidence of what unlocks one, so implementing it as a permanent exclusion would be a different parameter wearing this one's name — and would make a mission whose only capture objective is locked unwinnable. `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry` counts locked objectives and states in the boot log that the round runs as if every objective were live.

autoLose.description: When set, names the `factions[].key` that automatically LOSES if this objective falls. Absent or disabled is the dominant case, but the field is carried because live use of it exists in the source corpus. The semantics are inferred for the same reason as `lock`, so this is declared vocabulary rather than asserted behaviour. It is parsed and reported, deliberately not enforced: acting on it means ENDING A ROUND, and the round-end authority is `TBD_FrameworkManager.TickWinConditions` reading `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.EvaluateEndTriggers()` — one owner, in another file. The reader validates the key against `factions[].key` and blanks a dangling one, so a later consumer cannot inherit a side that does not exist.

variantId.description: Conditional inclusion. When set, this objective is emitted only if the named variant is selected.

objectiveFraming.description: One side's reading of an objective: its task title and body text, shown in that side's task tree. Both are optional, so a side may frame only a title or only text.

vehicle.description: One mission-placed vehicle (schemaVersion 1.3). `alias` is the `veh:` (or `comp:`) registry alias; `seats` carries the crew plan — which slots ride where — so the crew UI's authored state reaches the game. Crew spawn is read by the mission vehicle struct and seated by `TBD_SpawnManager`; `lock`, `fuel` and `ammo` are read by `TBD_VehicleState`. This is a first-class row, not an alias-substituted `entities[]` entry.

uid.description: Stable identity for this roster vehicle (schemaVersion 1.3), carried verbatim from the editor so a reference survives recompiles and edits — the same role `slot.uid` plays for a slot. A `get_in` waypoint's `vehicleUid` names this. Optional: a vehicle nothing references needs no uid. It is the join key the roster reader claims on, because one authored vehicle emits both this row and an `entities[]` alias row carrying the same uid, and only that claim stops the vehicle being spawned twice. A roster row with no uid falls back to an `alias|x|z` fingerprint.

seats.description: Crew assignment plan: which slot fills which crew position. `slotId` references `slots[].uid` — the durable identity, not the derived `id`; see the `slot.id` description on why references key on uid. `role` is the crew position. This is the seats-and-crew state the crew UI authors.

index.description: Disambiguates multiple positions of the same `role` (e.g. cargo seat 0, 1, 2…).

lock.description: Lock state on the roster vehicle (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_VehicleState` through `LockPilotControls`, and only when bound true, since a bool cannot distinguish an omitted key from an authored false.

variantId.description: Conditional inclusion. When set, this vehicle is emitted only if the named variant is selected.

editorTrigger.description: One editor-authored trigger (schemaVersion 1.3). Read the top-level `editorTriggers` description first, including why the key is not named `triggers`; `TBD_TriggerRuntime` reads it. An `activation` model (condition, repeat, timeout, owner side) fires an `effects` model. Geometry is a `zones[]` reference through `zoneId`, riding the zone draw tool rather than re-declaring a shape here: what this def owns is activation and effects, and the geometry and palette half lives elsewhere.

zoneId.description: The `zones[].id` whose volume arms this trigger. A trigger without a zone is a document-wide condition.

condition.description: What makes the trigger fire. Modelled on Eden's activation types; the closest existing TBD semantics are `$defs/zoneRules` (16 keys, the nearest thing TBD has to trigger semantics — read them before the reader lands).

ownerSide.description: Which faction's presence/detection the condition tests.

repeat.description: Whether the trigger re-arms after firing (Eden's repeatable flag).

timeoutSeconds.description: Delay between the condition holding and the effects firing.

effects.description: What happens when `activation` fires — an ordered list of effect records. `type` is the effect kind; `params` is an open bag the reader interprets (the effects vocabulary is a NEW Enfusion runtime, so its shape is deliberately not frozen into a closed enum here beyond the coarse `type`).

params.description: Effect-specific parameters, interpreted by the trigger runtime. Open by design — see the def description.

variantId.description: Conditional inclusion. When set, this trigger is emitted only if the named variant is selected.

variant.description: One named variant in the conditional-inclusion registry (schemaVersion 1.3). Read the top-level `variants` description first; `TBD_MissionLoader` reads this registry at parse. Declaring a variant here by `id` is what makes a `variantId` reference elsewhere validatable — an unknown id becomes a catchable error rather than a silent free string — which is the whole point of a central registry: it turns a by-hand layer-name convention into a checked contract.

id.description: Stable variant key, referenced by every subtree's `variantId`.

default.description: Whether this variant is selected when the launcher makes no choice.

variantIdRef.description: A reference to a `variants[].id`. The same shape as `variant.id`, so a subtree's `variantId` and the registry entry it points at cannot disagree on form. Whole-document referential integrity — every `variantId` naming a declared variant — is a graph check the mod-side reader owns, not something JSON Schema draft 2020-12 can express here: the pattern pins the SHAPE, which is the same split `entity.alias` uses, with the shape here and registry existence in the gate.

missionParam.description: One launch-time mission parameter (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_MissionParams`. It models Arma's `class Params` row: a named value chosen at launch, with a title key for i18n, the list of allowed values and their display strings, a default, and the symbol the mission consumes it through.

titleKey.description: i18n key for the launcher-facing title.

displays.description: Parallel display strings for `values` (Arma's `texts[]`). When present they must line up 1:1 with `values` — a length check the mission-params reader owns.

default.description: The value used when the launcher makes no choice. It must be one of `values` — a membership check the mission-params reader owns.

waypoint.description: One squad waypoint (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_WaypointRuntime` in both mod trees. Waypoints are ordered by position in the array; `type` is the waypoint kind and `x` / `z` its position. The AI spawn gate opens only for waypointed groups.

type.description: Waypoint kind — TBD vocabulary the reader maps onto whatever engine waypoint types Reforger exposes; the names here are the contract, not an engine identifier (no `SCR_AIWaypoint`-style family is asserted — verify the real engine types when the reader lands).

y.description: Optional waypoint height, metres ASL (same policy as `slot.y`).

vehicleUid.description: For a `get_in` waypoint — and, when boarding a specific vehicle, a `get_out` one — the target vehicle, referenced by a `vehicles[].uid`-style stable id, so the squad boards THE authored vehicle rather than any nearby one by proximity inference (schemaVersion 1.3). Absent falls back to nearest-by-proximity. Ignored for non-boarding waypoint types. Read by `TBD_WaypointRuntime`.

behaviour.description: Per-waypoint behaviour override (falls back to the group's `behaviour`).

speedMode.description: Per-waypoint speed override (falls back to the group's `speedMode`).

gadgetFlags.description: Per-player gadget presence flags (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_GadgetFlags`. Each is Eden's General-States gadget toggle: absent means leave the kit's default, while `true` and `false` force the gadget on or off. The reader uses a string-to-bool map so that an omitted key and an authored false do not collapse. The compiler omits the block on `/compiled`.

map.description: Spawn with a map. Read by `TBD_GadgetFlags`.

compass.description: Spawn with a compass. Read by `TBD_GadgetFlags`.

watch.description: Spawn with a watch. Read by `TBD_GadgetFlags`, which matches on the prefab path because the engine exposes no `EGadgetType.WATCH`.

gps.description: Spawn with a GPS. Read by `TBD_GadgetFlags`. An authored true cannot add a GPS, because the registry holds no GPS item; an authored false still withholds a GPS-named item.

radio.description: Spawn with a personal radio. Read by `TBD_GadgetFlags`.

winConditions.description: How the round is won. `endOn` is the closed list of triggers that may END the round: `TBD_ObjectiveRegistry.EvaluateEndTriggers` drives three of them and `TBD_FrameworkManager.TickWinConditions` the other two. `mode` is the authored win rule that sits on top of them. The enum carries seven values rather than five. The five the editor authors are `attrition`, `objective`, `extraction`, `vip` and `timeout` — the same five the compiler's authored-mode list and `mission-editor-payload.schema.json` declare, so an editor payload cannot carry the other two. `points_then_attrition` and `defender_holds_or_attacker_destroys` are grandfathered: they are not editor output and no slice emits them, but four committed hand-authored goldens (`bridgehead-at-levie`, `empty-warning-fields`, `slot-loadout-coverage`, `last-stand-at-montfort`) plus two invalid-golden fixtures carry them and must keep validating, so dropping them would fail schema validation on six committed files whose subject is the mod's parser rather than the win rule. They cost nothing at runtime: `mode` reaches the mod at exactly one place, `TBD_BriefingData.BuildWinConditions`, which renders `Humanise(mode)` on the briefing screen, and `TBD_WinConditionEvaluator` treats any mode outside the five as MODE_UNKNOWN, so the round ends on `endOn` alone. On per-mode params: `extractionZoneId`, `vipSlotId` and `timeoutMinutes` are each required by, and meaningful only to, one mode, which the `allOf` below states per mode rather than leaving three optional keys nothing has to fill in. The compiler additionally refuses a param belonging to a different mode than the one authored — a rule a schema `if`/`then` could express only as a fourth pile of conditionals — and names which param and which mode in the refusal.

mode.description: The authored win rule: five editor-authorable values plus two grandfathered golden-only values — see this block's own description for why the enum is seven wide. `attrition` is what the compiler emits when the payload authors no `winConditions` at all, which is what keeps a mission with no authored win rule byte-identical to one compiled before the key existed.

extractionZoneId.description:
The `zones[].id` an extracting side must reach. REQUIRED by `mode: extraction`; OPTIONAL on `mode: vip`, where it is what makes "the VIP got out" a thing the game can observe — without a zone, a VIP rule can only ever end on the VIP's death, which is half a rule. No other mode may carry it (`win_conditions.rs` refuses a param that belongs elsewhere).

`flatten.rs` reports a diagnostic when this names a zone that did not reach the wire, because an extraction zone that does not exist is a round that can never be won that way (the same rule `$defs/vehicle.seats[].slotId` follows against the emitted slots). Read by `TBD_WinConditionEvaluator`, which resolves it through `TBD_ZoneRegistry` and refuses to evaluate rather than inventing a zone.

vipSlotId.description: `mode: vip` only — the `slots[].uid` of the protected player. Matched against the EMITTED slot uids by `flatten.rs`, not the authored ones, for the same reason `$defs/vehicle.seats[].slotId` is: a uid that resolves in the editor payload but that the compile emitted no `slots[]` row for would dangle on the wire. Read by `TBD_WinConditionEvaluator`.

timeoutMinutes.description: `mode: timeout` only: how long the round runs before the clock ends it, in whole minutes. 1440 is 24 h, and the ceiling exists for the same reason `$defs/zoneRules.captureSeconds` has one — a typo'd `600` in place of `60` is a round nobody can finish. It is not a second clock: the compiler projects it onto `flow.timeLimitSeconds` (multiplied by 60) and adds `time_limit` to `endOn`, so the round is ended by the one armed clock `TBD_FrameworkManager.ArmRoundClock` already runs. Two timers for one deadline is a defect class of its own, and `TBD_WinConditionEvaluator` deliberately starts no timer for this mode.

task.description: One authored task. Transitions are assigned → succeeded and assigned → failed only; anything else is logged and ignored, and the server is authoritative through `TBD_TaskStateMachine`. `triggerId` names an `editorTriggers[].id` whose completion drives the success transition. `markerId` is the HUD glyph: an authored `$defs/marker.icon` alias resolved through `TBD_MarkerIcons`, the same path markers use. Position comes from the linked trigger's zone.

title.description: The words on the HUD marker and in the tasks panel.

state.description: Authoring default is `assigned`. The runtime writes the terminal state; the editor may also author a terminal state for a task that has already resolved in a canned scenario.

triggerId.description: Optional `editorTriggers[].id`. When that trigger fires, an `assigned` task becomes `succeeded`. An inert or missing trigger fails the task. Tasks observe; they never fire endOn.

markerId.description: Optional HUD icon alias from `$defs/marker.icon` (TBD_MarkerIcons.Register keys). Absent ⇒ the HUD uses `objective_marker`.

description.description: Optional longer briefing text. Not drawn on the HUD marker.

schedule.description: Optional timed window. Absent means untimed — the task is always evaluated. `TBD_TaskStateMachine` reads the nested `startAfterS` and `windowS` through an ABSENT sentinel, so presence of the object is not itself a nested-ref test.

taskSchedule.description: A timed window measured from mission start: `startAfterS` seconds of delay and `windowS` seconds of duration. `windowS` must be greater than 0, and `startAfterS` must be at least 0 and strictly inside the mission length — both enforced by the compiler, while the schema pins the types and closes the key set.

startAfterS.description: Seconds from mission start before the task becomes active. 0 is legal and means evaluate from T+0.

windowS.description: Duration in seconds that the task stays evaluable after `startAfterS`. Must be greater than 0.

weatherTimeline.description: Authored weather KEYFRAMES (schemaVersion 1.3). Distinct from `environment.weatherPreset`, the single static preset the mission starts with. A timeline is `{keyframes: [{atMinutes, weatherPreset, windDirDeg?, fog?}]}`; `atMinutes` is minutes from LIVE start and must be strictly increasing, which the compiler enforces while the schema pins the types and closes the key set. The preset vocabulary is the same four strings `environment.weatherPreset` uses: `clear`, `overcast`, `heavy_rain`, `dense_fog`. Read by `TBD_WeatherRuntime` in both mod trees: the server applies each keyframe at its offset through `TimeAndWeatherManagerEntity.ForceWeatherTo`, and clients follow weather replication. An absent object means a mission with no timeline, and the authored-block carrier then emits nothing, so byte-parity fixtures stay identical.

weatherKeyframe.description: One authored weather keyframe. `TBD_WeatherRuntime` applies `weatherPreset` at `atMinutes` and, when present, the fog and wind-direction overrides.

atMinutes.description: Minutes from LIVE start. 0 is legal (apply immediately when the round goes live). Strictly increasing across `keyframes[]` (weather.rs).

weatherPreset.description: Same vocabulary as environment.weatherPreset / flatten.rs WEATHER_PRESETS / weather.rs WEATHER_PRESETS.

windDirDeg.description: Optional wind direction, on the same axis as `environment.windDirDeg`. Omitted leaves the previous override — or the static environment value — alone.

fog.description: Optional fog density, on the same axis as `environment.fog`. Omitted leaves the previous override alone.

audio.description: Authored positional AUDIO emitters and music cues (schemaVersion 1.3). `emitters[]` are world-space sound sources `{id, x, z, y?, sound, radiusM, loop, triggerId?}`; `musicCues[]` are `{id, event, track}` fired on mission_start, task_succeeded, task_failed or mission_end. `radiusM` must be greater than 0, which the schema pins with `exclusiveMinimum` and the compiler re-checks. Ids are unique across both arrays. Read by `TBD_AudioEmitter` in both mod trees: the server arms emitters (honouring `triggerId`) and plays cues on the named events, while each client spawns one sound source per emitter and raises the sound only while the local player is inside `radiusM`. An absent object means a mission with no authored audio, and the authored-block carrier then emits nothing, so byte-parity fixtures stay identical.

audioEmitter.description: One positional sound source. `TBD_AudioEmitter` spawns a client-side source at (x, z) — at `y` metres ASL when authored, otherwise on the terrain surface — and raises `sound` only while the listener is inside `radiusM`. `loop` keeps it repeating inside the radius; a one-shot fires once on first entry. `triggerId` delays arming until that `editorTriggers[]` row has fired; omitted arms at LIVE.

id.description: Stable emitter id. Unique across `audio.emitters[]` and `audio.musicCues[]`.

y.description: Optional height, metres ASL. Omitted ⇒ terrain surface at (x, z).

sound.description: `SCR_SoundEvent` name, the same vocabulary a trigger's play-sound effect uses. An unknown name raises nothing.

radiusM.description: Hearable radius in metres. Must be > 0 (audio.rs radius_above_zero).

loop.description: When true, the source repeats while the listener stays inside radiusM. When false, it fires once on first enter. Absent and false are indistinguishable at JsonLoadContext (bools have no sentinel); default is false.

triggerId.description: Optional `editorTriggers[].id`. The emitter stays silent until that trigger FIRED. A missing id is logged and the emitter never arms.

musicCue.description: One 2D music or UI cue fired on a named mission event. `track` is an `SCR_SoundEvent` name; `event` is the closed vocabulary below.

id.description: Stable cue id. Unique across `audio.emitters[]` and `audio.musicCues[]`.

event.description: When the cue plays. mission_start is LIVE entry; mission_end is END entry; task_succeeded / task_failed fire when TBD_TaskStateMachine commits that transition (any task).

track.description: `SCR_SoundEvent` name raised as a 2D cue, on the same path a trigger's play-sound effect uses.

spawnModule.description: One dynamic spawn module. `TBD_DynamicSpawner` spawns `count` groups of `groupTemplate` for `factionKey`. Placement is exclusive: either world `(x, z)` or a `zones[].id` through `zoneId`, never both and never neither, which the compiler's placement check enforces. `kind: wave` restocks on `intervalSeconds` while living groups stay below `maxAlive`, itself capped at 32. `kind: garrison` spawns once and holds. `triggerId` delays the first spawn until that `editorTriggers[]` row has fired; omitted arms at LIVE.

kind.description: wave restocks on an interval up to maxAlive; garrison spawns once and holds.

factionKey.description: Must be one of blufor / opfor / indfor / civ (spawn_modules.rs FACTION_KEYS, same keys TBD_SpawnManager.EngineFactionKey maps).

groupTemplate.description: AI group prefab resource name (e.g. `{GUID}Prefabs/AI/Groups/...et`). Unknown resources log and skip at runtime.

x.description: World X metres. Required with `z` when `zoneId` is omitted.

z.description: World Z metres. Required with `x` when `zoneId` is omitted.

zoneId.description: Optional `zones[].id`. The module spawns at that zone's centre. Exclusive with x/z.

count.description: Groups to spawn per volley (wave) or once (garrison). Must be > 0 and ≤ 32.

intervalSeconds.description: Wave restock interval in seconds. Must be > 0 when present. Omitted on a wave ⇒ spawn one volley only. Ignored for garrison.

maxAlive.description: Wave: do not spawn while living groups ≥ this cap. Omitted ⇒ `count`. Hard-capped at 32. Ignored for garrison.

triggerId.description: Optional `editorTriggers[].id`. First spawn waits until that trigger FIRED. A missing id is logged and the module never arms.

tacticalGraphic.description: One tactical control measure: an ORDERED RUN of world vertices with a doctrinal kind. Deliberately not `#/$defs/polygon`, which is `minItems: 3` and closed — these are OPEN polylines and a two-point phase line is the commonest case there is. `style` reuses the marker vocabulary rather than inventing a second one (`color` is `#/$defs/hexColor`, `alpha` is 0..1, `brush` is the same eight Eden fill names `$defs/marker.brush` declares), so a reader that already styles markers styles these from the same table. `widthM` is the one addition, and the geometry forces it: a marker is a glyph with a `size` multiplier, whereas a control measure is a STROKE and a stroke needs a world width. Vertex-count floors are per kind and are enforced by the compiler's `min_points` rather than by this schema, because JSON Schema cannot make `minItems` depend on a sibling's value without an `if`/`then` per kind, and keeping the rule in one Rust function keeps the refusal a sentence the author can read.

kind.description: phase_line = a control line units report crossing; boundary = the seam between two sides' areas of responsibility; axis_of_advance = a straight direction of attack; curved_arrow = the same intent along a curve, drawn Catmull-Rom through `points`. The first three need ≥ 2 vertices, `curved_arrow` needs ≥ 3 (see `$defs/tacticalGraphic`'s note on min_points).

points.description: World `[x, z]` vertices in author order. `minItems` is the floor common to every kind; the per-kind floor (3 for `curved_arrow`) is `tactical_graphics.rs` `min_points`. `maxItems` mirrors MAX_POINTS.

label.description: Optional map label — "PL BLUE", "AXIS SABRE". `wireSafeString` for the same delimited-wire reason every other authored label is.

sideKey.description: Optional owning side — a `factions[].key`. A PATTERN and not an enum because faction keys are authored; whether the key names a faction that exists is a cross-block question the document validator owns, not this block's.

tacticalGraphicStyle.description: Optional stroke style for a tactical graphic. Every key is optional; an absent `style` means the renderer picks its own defaults from `sideKey`, which is the common case and the reason nothing here is required.

color.description: Stroke colour, the same `#rrggbb` form `marker.color` and `faction.color` use.

alpha.description: Opacity, 0 (transparent) → 1 (opaque). Same range and meaning as `marker.alpha`.

brush.description: Fill brush, spelled identically to `marker.brush` so one reader can style both from one table.

widthM.description: Stroke width in world metres. The one key with no marker counterpart — a marker is a glyph scaled by `size`, a control measure is a stroke with a width.

icon.description: Authored marker glyph alias. Closed vocabulary, matching the 64 `Register()` keys in `TBD_MarkerIcons.EnsureAliases` — the words a mission author or the Mission Creator may type. Without the enum a typo or an empty string validates clean and then degrades at runtime: `Resolve()` returns FALLBACK_ICON (DOT) and logs once, so the marker still draws, but not as authored. Live engine imageset-quad names may still resolve at RUNTIME through the config-quad path, but the AUTHORED contract is this enum only, so a document that passes the validator never needs the silent DOT downgrade.

size.description: Marker icon and text scale multiplier, where 1 is the default (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct` in `TBD_MissionLoader`, packed onto the marker RPC trailer and applied by `TBD_MarkerClient`. The entity `size` key is a different field that shares this spelling.

rotationDeg.description: Marker rotation in degrees (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct` and applied through `TBD_MarkerClient.SetRotation`.

shape.description: Icon-versus-AREA is Eden's entire second marker model, and this key is the ICON-side selector and authoring hint, not the geometry (schemaVersion 1.3). Precedence is the one rule that resolves the two: if `area` (a `#/$defs/markerArea`) is present, this marker IS an area marker and `shape` is IGNORED — the authoritative extent is `area`, whose vocabulary (circle, polygon, rectangle, ellipse) is the superset that can actually express a rect or ellipse. If `area` is absent, this is an icon marker and the `icon` glyph is drawn. `icon` names the glyph marker; `rectangle`, `ellipse` and `polyline` are shape hints subordinate to `area`, so an author who sets `shape: "ellipse"` must also author an ellipse `area` for it to take effect, and a mismatch resolves in `area`'s favour by this rule. Read by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct.shape`. Area FILL over `area` geometry is not drawn, because `SCR_MapMarkerBase` has no brush API; the mod logs once and still draws the icon with the authored colour, rotation, size and alpha.

brush.description: Area-marker fill brush, matching Eden's marker brush set (schemaVersion 1.3). Meaningful only for a `shape` other than `icon`. Read by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct.brush`, which binds and packs it; the fill is not painted on the map widget.

color.description: Marker colour, in the same `#rrggbb` form as `faction.color` (schemaVersion 1.3). Read by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct.color`; the hex value is mapped to the nearest `SCR_EScenarioFrameworkMarkerCustomColor` through `SetColorEntry`.

alpha.description: Marker opacity, 0 (transparent) to 1 (opaque), schemaVersion 1.3. Read by `TBD_MissionMarkerStruct.alpha` and applied as `TBD_StyledMapMarker` widget opacity.

area.description: The AUTHORITATIVE extent of an area marker (schemaVersion 1.3): circle, polygon, rectangle or ellipse, through `#/$defs/markerArea` — a superset of the zone `#/$defs/shape` that adds the rect and ellipse extents `shape`'s circle-or-polygon vocabulary cannot express. Precedence: when `area` is present this marker is an AREA marker and `marker.shape` is ignored; the rule is stated once here and once on `shape`. Its circle and polygon arms speak the same geometry vocabulary as a zone, so an area marker and a zone stay comparable. On the wire only; no mod-side reader binds it.

spectatorPolicy.description: Who may enter spectator, and when. Read by `TBD_SpectatorController` through the replicated `TBD_FrameworkManager.GetSpectatorPolicy()`. Empty or unauthored keeps the enter-immediately behaviour.

nightVision.description: Whether night-vision gadgets are allowed. Read by `TBD_FrameworkManager`, which strips NVG gadgets when the value is false. `JsonLoadContext` binds an omitted key as false, so a mission that does not author the key has its NVG stripped.
